title: PH to seek reduction of 12.5% tariff on US exports during Trump visit
summary: The Philippine government will be lobbying for the reduction of 12.5% tariff on Philippine goods entering the United States during the state visit of US President Donald Trump to the country.

blocks.text: The Philippine government will be lobbying for the reduction of 12.5% tariff on Philippine goods entering the United States during the state visit of US President Donald Trump to the country.

"Of course, my wish is to bring down the tariff," Trade and Industry Secretary Ma. Cristina Roque said at the sidelines of a press conference following the conclusion of the 28th Association of the Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Economic Community Council in Pasay City on Monday.
The Trade chief was asked if Manila will negotiate for the reduction of the 12.5% tariff slapped on Philippine exports to America.
Last July, the US announced a new tariff rate of 12.5% for Philippine goods due to the country's alleged failure to curb the importation of goods produced with forced labor.
Roque, however, declined to disclose by how much the Philippine side wants the tariff rate reduced.
"We want to be able to expand the exports to the US and to all other markets globally," she said.
"I don't want to disclose any information regarding the meeting," she added, noting that "it's already in the 18th [November]… we will bring up."
In a message to GMA News Online, Roque said, "We do not want to speculate on the results of the discussions between the leaders at this point in time."
Since February, Philippine goods entering the US were subject to a 10% baseline tariff after the US Supreme Court declared US President Donald Trump's reciprocal tariff policy as unconstitutional.
The 10% baseline tariff expired Friday, July 24, allowing the US government to impose fresh duties following its investigation into trading-partner countries' forced labor imports.
Data from the Office of the US Trade Representative showed US goods trade with the Philippines totaled an estimated $26.9 billion in 2025.
US goods exports to the Philippines stood at $9.1 billion last year, down 1.1% year-on-year, while its goods imports from the Philippines amounted $17.8 billion, up 25.4%.
The US goods trade deficit with the Philippines was $8.6 billion in 2025, a 75.3% increase, according to USTR. — VDV, GMA News
